ghcr.io/stacklok/dockyard/npx/brightdata.overview:
## Bright Data MCP Server

The brightdata-mcp server is a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that enables AI assistants and agents to access real-time web data through Bright Data's global proxy and scraping infrastructure. It allows AI workflows to fetch live web content, extract structured data, and perform large-scale web data collection without building or maintaining custom scraping systems. This makes it ideal for research, market analysis, competitive intelligence, and any AI-driven workflow that depends on fresh, publicly available web data.

tool_definitions.description: Ask Bright Data's support assistant (Sophie) a question about Bright Data products, APIs, MCP usage, zones, scraping, or account setup. Use when the user asks "how do I..." about Bright Data, when you hit a Bright Data error you don't recognize, or when deciding between products (Web Unlocker vs. Scraping Browser vs. dataset tools). Supports threaded follow-ups via dialog_id.

question.description: The question to ask. Max 20480 chars.

tool_definitions.name: ask_brightdata_assistant

tool_definitions.description:
Find companies or people (LinkedIn data) by description or criteria. Ranked results in one call. First choice to find companies or people.
Up to 10 records per call; each call is billed.
Result: JSON with meta and documents. meta.matched is a lower bound, not a total. meta.coverage_percent below 100 means a partial result. Empty documents means no match, not that the company or person does not exist. A missing field means no stored value.

limit.description: Records per call, 1-10, default 10. With view full: 5 or less.

mode.description:
How the query runs. Default instant.
instant: query is plain text. An AI planner turns it into filters and ranks the matches. Use it for most questions.
smart: as instant, then an AI reranks the best 50 matches for fit to the question. Slower and costs more. Use it when the order matters, for example "the best fit" or "the most relevant".
ludicrous: query is a JSON object (see query). Exact filters, no AI, fastest. Use it when you know the fields and values, when instant gives wrong matches, or to page past 100 matches.

offset.description: Records to skip, default 0. For the next page, add limit to offset. instant and smart: offset+limit 100 or less. ludicrous: offset 1000 or less.

query.description:
instant and smart: plain text, 1-200 characters, for example "fintech startups in Berlin". ludicrous: a JSON object.
Operators: {"and": [..]}, {"or": [..]}, {"not": cond}, {"equals": {field: value}}, {"in": {field: [values]}}, {"range": {field: {">=": n, "<=": n}}}, {"text": {field: "words"}} or {"text": {field: {"value": "words", "mode": "all"}}}.
Example: {"and": [{"text": {"industry": "software"}}, {"in": {"headquarters_country_code": ["US", "GB"]}}]}
Company fields. text: name industry about slogan specialties headquarters_location. equals/in: headquarters_country_code funding_stage. equals: headquarters_city organization_type. in: offices_country_codes offices_cities. range: employees_in_linkedin company_size_from company_size_to funding_raised linkedin_followers. range/equals: founded_year.
People fields. text: name current_title about location current_company_name current_company_industry past_job_titles past_company_names certification_names education_schools education_details all_text role company skill. equals/in: city country_code linkedin_person_id. range: current_tenure_months followers. range/equals/in: experience_years.
Each field list belongs to one category.

view.description:
Which fields each record returns. Default summary.
summary: the main fields.
  company: company_id url name slogan about industry specialties organization_type company_size_from company_size_to founded_year headquarters_location headquarters_country_code offices_cities linkedin_followers employees_in_linkedin funding_stage funding_raised domain website logo scraped_at.
  people: name url current_title current_company_name current_tenure_months about past_job_titles location city country_code experience_years followers connections.
full: all fields, the summary fields plus others, for example the fields below. Records are large: use limit 5 or less.
  company: headquarters_city offices_country_codes offices_addresses directions_urls alumni_count alumni_information linkedin_follower_to_employee_ratio investor_names crunchbase_id image linkedin_id.
  people: first_name recommendations_count recommendations influencer patent_count past_company_names education_schools education_details certification_names languages current_company_industry current_company_specialties current_company_description current_company_slogan current_company_headquarters current_company_country_code current_company_size_from current_company_size_to current_company_funding_stage current_company_funding_raised avatar linkedin_num_id linkedin_person_id.
{"fields": [..]}: only the named fields, any of the summary or full fields of the category. The smallest result. Example for people: {"fields": ["name", "url", "current_title", "current_company_name"]}.

tool_definitions.description:
Fetch one web page. Returns JSON: url, format, content, plus title and note when present. content is the page in one format, markdown by default. Pick another with the format param:
- text: plain text, no links or headings
- html: raw HTML, for CSS selectors or data hidden in the markup
- ld_json: schema.org data (price, rating, author...)
If the page has no data in that format, markdown is returned instead, with a note. No JavaScript rendering. Pages that take longer than 45 s time out. Pages over 40,000 characters are cut. To read the rest for free, call again with the snapshot_id and start values from the result's next field.

snapshot_id.description: From next in a cut result

start.description: Character offset to read from, from next

tool_definitions.name: scrape_as_markdown

tool_definitions.description:
Fetch up to 5 web pages at once. Returns a JSON array in input order, one item per URL: url, format, content, plus title and note when present; or url and error if that page failed. content is the page in one format, markdown by default. Pick another with the format param:
- text: plain text, no links or headings
- html: raw HTML, for CSS selectors or data hidden in the markup
- ld_json: schema.org data (price, rating, author...)
If a page has no data in that format, markdown is returned instead, with a note. No JavaScript rendering. Pages that take longer than 35 s time out (45 s when only one URL is sent). The whole result is cut at 40,000 characters, shared between pages. To read the rest of a cut page for free, call scrape_as_markdown with its url and the snapshot_id and start values from that item's next field.

tool_definitions.description:
Exact filters on raw LinkedIn dataset fields, the contact-enriched people dataset, or when business_search is not enabled for this account. To find companies or people by description or criteria.
First call list_dataset_fields to get valid field names.
A filter is a tree: a group {operator:"and"|"or", filters:[...]} or a leaf {name, value, operator}. Max nesting depth 3.
Leaf operators: =, !=, <, <=, >, >=, in, not_in, includes, not_includes, array_includes, not_array_includes, is_null, is_not_null.
Supported dataset_id values:
- gd_l1viktl72bvl7bjuj0: LinkedIn people profiles
- gd_me5ppxjr2ge6icjuh0: LinkedIn people profiles (contact-enriched)
- gd_l1vikfnt1wgvvqz95w: LinkedIn company information

operator.description: Filter operator, one of: =, !=, <, <=, >, >=, in, not_in, includes, not_includes, array_includes, not_array_includes, is_null, is_not_null

value.description: Value to compare against. Omit for is_null / is_not_null.
